findings.text: No delegated agent begins from nowhere. A position is authored before it is occupied: an intention has acquired a task, a vocabulary, permissions and criteria under which someone else can act. The author does not thereby determine every consequence. Authored ground gives the delegate a place from which to judge; positional delegation makes that judgment effective within a bounded scope.

findings.why_necessary: Intention must become a finite formulated task before it can be delegated; consequence exceeds that first formulation.
findings.stronger_inference_if_removed: Removing the consequence distinction would make original written wording exhaust the living purpose or deny real delegate judgment.
findings.positive_operation_retained: Authored ground gives bounded real judgment with answerable relation to purpose.

findings.text: The practical return concerns the terms of commission. A delegate can meet contradictory evidence, unforeseen cost or a better possibility. A finished answer leaves these discoveries ineffective when they cannot reach the interpretation, criterion or authorised route implicated by the encounter. The delegation becomes answerable where the encountered difference can return to the position which framed it.

findings.complete_paragraph: Within [covenantal delegation](A25-prime-Covenant-Architecture.md), an occupant exercises a received grant; replacement does not erase that commissioning relation.
